messages.subject: variables now scoped
parts:
Variables are now all scoped. I had to change
several of the BUGS models to comply.

Specifically, a variable may only be set (that
is, act on the LHS of an assignment statment, x <- ...),
in its own block.

Local variables in scope (each is scoped to its block)
are always assignable. Otherwise, derived data and
derived parameter variables may only be set in their
respective blocks.

The biggest consequence of this is that derived
parameters MUST be defined in the derived parameter
block. They can't be set later in the model. (The
effect would be the same in terms of computation,
but enforcing derived parameter scope will make the
models clearer and also allow me to not run the model
code when writing output [not really a big deal]).

Here's a test case with an example of LEGAL assignments
(from the test suite, of course).

---------------------------------
data {
double a;
}
derived data {
double b;
b <- 1.0;
b <- a + b + 1.0;
{
double b_local; // init to 0 locally
b <- a + b + b_local;
b_local <- a + b + b_local;

}
}
parameters {
double c;
}
derived parameters {
double d;
d <- 1.0;
d <- a + b + c + d;
{
double d_local;
d <- a + b + c + d + d_local;
d_local <- a + b + c + d + d_local;
}
}
model {
double e_local;
e_local <- 1.0;
e_local <- a + b + c + d + e_local;
{
double f_local;
f_local <- 1.0;
e_local <- a + b + c + d + e_local + f_local;
f_local <- a + b + c + d + e_local + f_local;
}
}
generated quantities {
double g;
g <- 1.0;
g <- a + b + c + d + g;
{
double g_local;
g_local <- 1.0;
g <- a + b + c + d + g + g_local;
g_local <- a + b + c + d + g + g_local;
}
}
---------------------------------

- Bob
